newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: HG Asia, joint venture apply for Seoul bourse seats.
newsitem.headline: HG Asia, joint venture apply for Seoul bourse seats.

text.p: HG Asia Securities Ltd and a South Korean-U.S. joint venture have applied for seats on the Korea Stock Exchange, an exchange statement said on Friday.
HG Asia has applied for a special membership, which does not carry voting rights.
If accepted, it would become the fourth foreign member on the exchange after Jardine Fleming Securities, ING Baring Securities and Morgan Stanley Securities.
KEB-SB Securities Co Ltd, which is 51 percent held by the Korea Exchange Bank and 49 percent by Smith Barney Inc, has applied for a full membership.

"Joining the stock exchange helps up your profile and show South Korea your long-term commitment," said HG Asia's branch manager Keith Nam. "You also bypass the 30 percent commission paid to local brokers, so medium to long term it's profitable."
KEB-SB hopes to become the third joint venture member, after Dongbang Peregrine Securities and Hannuri-Salomon Securities.
Special membership fees on the bourse comes to $5.0 million, while a full membership costs $20 million.
